content_voiceover: This page covers two questions, one on a recent clinical trial and one on ELN 2022 risk stratification. Question thirty nine references a 2025 Blood paper comparing venetoclax plus decitabine against intensive chemotherapy as induction in young patients with newly diagnosed AML, and asks which description is wrong. The answer is the statement claiming infection rates were similar between the two groups, when in fact the trial showed differences in infection risk between the venetoclax decitabine arm and the intensive chemotherapy arm. The other statements, about similar remission rates overall, a higher composite remission rate in adverse risk or U2AF1 mutated patients with venetoclax decitabine, lower serious adverse events, and similar one year event free survival, are all accurate per the trial. Question nineteen asks which statement about ELN 2022 risk stratification is wrong, and the answer involves NPM1 mutated AML with the translocation between chromosomes six and nine producing the DEK NUP214 fusion. Even though NPM1 mutation alone is typically favorable, the DEK NUP214 fusion is itself an adverse risk defining lesion, so this combination should be classified as adverse risk, not intermediate risk as the statement claims.
keypoints: VEN-DEC vs intensive chemo trial: infection incidence actually differed, not similar
VEN-DEC showed higher CRc in ELN-2022 adverse-risk or U2AF1-mutated patients
DEK::NUP214 fusion from t(6;9) is adverse-risk defining even with NPM1 mutation present
NPM1 mutation alone does not override an adverse cytogenetic partner lesion
keypoint_voiceover: Two takeaways, in the 2025 venetoclax decitabine trial infection rates were not simply similar between arms. And under ELN 2022, DEK NUP214 fusion keeps a case adverse risk even when NPM1 is mutated, since that translocation trumps the favorable NPM1 signal.
